# Incident Report — MTA-2026-02-28 Packet Capture Analysis

## Evidence reviewed
- `2026-02-28-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (15,512 frames, capture start 2026-02-28 23:55:06 UTC+4)
- No IDS/Suricata alert exports were present in the evidence directory; findings below are derived entirely from the packet capture using tshark.

## Victim host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.2.28.88 |
| MAC | 00:19:d1:b2:4d:ad (Intel) |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-TEYQ2NR |
| AD domain | EASYAS123.TECH (DC: EASYAS123-DC.easyas123.tech, 10.2.28.2) |
| Logged-in user | brolf (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString to the DC) |

## Malware family
**NetSupport RAT** (malicious use of the NetSupport Manager remote-access client). Attribution is **behavioral/network-signature based, not AV/hash-confirmed** — no dropper executable or antivirus/YARA verdict was recoverable from this capture (the infection vector itself is not present in the pcap; only post-infection C2 is). The call is based on:
- Every C2 POST uses the literal User-Agent `NetSupport Manager/1.3`.
- Every request hits the same static path, `/fakeurl.htm`, a well-known NetSupport RAT check-in endpoint.
- Traffic body format follows the NetSupport RAT client-gateway protocol: `CMD=POLL / INFO=1 / ACK=1` polling frames, answered by `CMD=ENCD / ES=1 / DATA=<encrypted blob>` from the server — i.e., an encrypted tunnel disguised as ordinary form POSTs.
- The C2 channel runs on TCP/443 but is plaintext HTTP, not TLS — a deliberate port/protocol mismatch to blend into outbound firewall allow-rules for 443.

## Timeline
- 23:55:50.9 — victim browses `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` (legitimate Akamai-hosted .gov site, real TLS handshake, SNI confirmed) — consistent with a DOT/FMCSA-compliance-themed social-engineering lure (a "ClickFix"-style fake verification prompt is the typical delivery chain for this family).
- 23:55:51.2–51.3 — victim resolves `vadusa.xyz` → `45.131.214.85`.
- 23:55:51.5 — first C2 POST to `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm` fires, within one second of the DNS lookup.
- C2 beaconing continues for the remainder of the capture (~250+ POSTs, last one at frame 15499), roughly every 10–60 seconds.

## Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in traffic)

**C2 endpoint**
- `45.131.214.85:443` (HTTP over TCP/443, not TLS)

**Malicious domain**
- `vadusa.xyz` → resolves to 45.131.214.85 (confirmed via DNS A record, frame 2566)

**Malicious URL**
- `http://45.131.214.85/fakeurl.htm` (POST, NetSupport RAT check-in/beacon endpoint)

**Transferred files / hashes**
- None. No executable, script, or other payload was captured being downloaded or exfiltrated in this pcap — all C2 body content observed is the encrypted `DATA=` blob inside the POLL/ENCD protocol frames. No file names or SHA256 hashes can be grounded in this evidence; do not report any.

## Notes / non-findings worth flagging
- `www.fmcsa.dot.gov` (23.64.147.24, Akamai) itself shows a legitimate TLS session — it is circumstantial (temporal proximity to infection), not independently confirmed malicious in this capture.
- `acroipm2.adobe.com GET /assets/Owner/arm/ProcessMAU.txt` used an anomalous, very old spoofed User-Agent (MSIE 7.0/Windows NT 6.2) but resolves to a legitimate Adobe/Akamai IP and returned no exportable object; insufficient evidence to call it malicious.
- All other DNS/HTTP/TLS activity (Microsoft telemetry, Windows Update, MSN, Bing, Office, Skype, Adobe, NVIDIA, Google) is consistent with normal enterprise workstation background noise and shows no other indicators of compromise.
